rows.notes: The cited document is a systematic (narrative) review of 148 records on climate change impacts on coffee; it reports no own data, experiment or model runs (Section 4 states the team opted for a narrative synthesis). It does not evaluate drip or sensor-based irrigation at all; irrigation appears only as a keyword in the PICO outcome list. No evidence on drip irrigation as a drought-risk adaptation.

Same review document; no primary data. Neither rainwater harvesting nor micro-irrigation is examined or discussed as an adaptation measure in the text; the review's own content concerns yield, suitability, pests/diseases, physiology, CO2 and socio-economic impacts of climate change on coffee.

notes: The document is a systematic review (Plants 2023, 12, 102), not a primary study. Its text is duplicated in places due to PDF extraction overlap but appears complete. It contains no mention of drip, sensor-based or micro-irrigation or rainwater harvesting beyond 'irrigation' as a search keyword, so it cannot support either claim.
